provenance.description: Hand-authored fictional contrast cases for regression. These are not actual papers, fresh biological findings, reader judgments, or evidence of scientific quality or production accuracy. Labels encode proposed contribution boundaries rather than personal relevance ground truth.
provenance.comparison_contract: Hold each contrast family together if a future separately declared synthetic experiment is authorized. These regression cases are never silently merged into real calibration or fresh evaluation.
provenance.validation_meaning: Fictional validation claims in supplied text; separate from scope and contribution role. They do not establish real quality.
provenance.uncertainty_contract: Ambiguous ownership or unspecified contribution remains uncertain; domain words alone cannot establish a contribution.

examples.title: Fictional transferable protein conformation predictor
examples.abstract: We introduce a transferable model that predicts protein conformational changes from sequence and molecular context. Evaluation on held-out protein families tests generalization rather than describing one native structure.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce a transferable model that predicts protein conformational changes from sequence and molecular context.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce and evaluate a molecular prediction method
examples.rationale: The method itself predicts molecular properties and is evaluated across independent families.

examples.title: Fictional application of a protein conformation predictor
examples.abstract: We apply an existing model that predicts protein conformational changes to describe a single native enzyme. The study interprets the resulting conformations and does not evaluate a new predictor or a transferable benchmark.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We apply an existing model that predicts protein conformational changes to describe a single native enzyme.
examples.contribution_task: Use an existing predictor for a descriptive case study
examples.rationale: Protein prediction is a tool used for natural-system description rather than the transferable contribution.

examples.title: Fictional assistant for protein literature questions
examples.abstract: We introduce a new language-model assistant that retrieves protein papers and summarizes their reported conclusions. Its outputs are cited prose answers, not predicted molecular structures, functions, or engineered sequences.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce a new language-model assistant that retrieves protein papers and summarizes their reported conclusions.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce a literature retrieval and summarization assistant
examples.rationale: A new method about protein literature does not by itself constitute molecular prediction or design.

examples.title: Fictional language model for protein function prediction
examples.abstract: We introduce a new language-model predictor that estimates molecular functions for previously unseen protein sequences. Its outputs are molecular function predictions, and held-out families test whether those predictions transfer beyond the training examples.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce a new language-model predictor that estimates molecular functions for previously unseen protein sequences.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce a transferable molecular function predictor
examples.rationale: The prediction target is a molecular property rather than prose or literature records.

examples.title: Fictional RNA assay for diagnostic risk estimation
examples.abstract: We introduce an RNA abundance assay and a classifier that estimates a patient's diagnostic risk from measured transcripts. The reported outputs are clinical risk categories; the work does not construct RNA architectures or develop molecular folding predictions.
examples.label: off_interest
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce an RNA abundance assay and a classifier that estimates a patient's diagnostic risk from measured transcripts.
examples.contribution_object: Clinical risk categories from transcript measurements
examples.contribution_task: Introduce a diagnostic assay and risk classifier
examples.rationale: RNA is measured as an analyte; the contribution concerns diagnostics rather than engineered RNA devices.

examples.title: Fictional programmable RNA nanodevice
examples.abstract: We engineer an RNA nanodevice with a deliberately specified folding architecture and reversible mechanical response. The study compares intended and observed device behavior, making the designed RNA system the central contribution.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We engineer an RNA nanodevice with a deliberately specified folding architecture and reversible mechanical response.
examples.contribution_object: An engineered RNA architecture and its device behavior
examples.contribution_task: Design and characterize a programmable RNA system
examples.rationale: The designed architecture and operating principle are the object of the study.

examples.title: Fictional designed condensate material
examples.abstract: We engineer synthetic condensate materials whose assembly and mechanical response follow specified design goals. The results compare designed variants and their controllable material behavior rather than explaining one cellular condensate.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We engineer synthetic condensate materials whose assembly and mechanical response follow specified design goals.
examples.contribution_task: Engineer condensate assembly and material behavior
examples.rationale: The engineered assembly and functional response establish a materials design contribution.

examples.title: Fictional mechanism of a natural cellular condensate
examples.abstract: We characterize how an endogenous cellular condensate changes during a native signaling response. The contribution explains the natural mechanism; no new material architecture, controllable assembly rule, or general design method is introduced.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We characterize how an endogenous cellular condensate changes during a native signaling response.
examples.contribution_task: Explain a natural assembly mechanism
examples.rationale: Natural condensate mechanisms remain context when they supply no transferable design contribution.

examples.title: Fictional review of molecular design predictors
examples.abstract: This review summarizes published protein design and structure prediction methods and compares their stated limitations. It synthesizes existing reports without introducing a predictor, engineering a new molecular system, or providing a new transferable evaluation benchmark.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: This review summarizes published protein design and structure prediction methods and compares their stated limitations.
examples.contribution_task: Review and synthesize existing reports
examples.rationale: Scope vocabulary in a review does not imply an original molecular engineering method.

examples.title: Fictional original molecular design predictor
examples.abstract: We introduce a protein design predictor and evaluate its generated structures across independently held-out families. A discussion of published methods provides background, while the new predictor and its evaluation are the contribution of this study.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce a protein design predictor and evaluate its generated structures across independently held-out families.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce and evaluate a molecular design predictor
examples.rationale: The original method remains the contribution even when the abstract also discusses prior literature.

examples.title: Fictional externally validated forest risk predictor
examples.abstract: We introduce a forest fire risk predictor and validate it prospectively at independent sites with rigorous uncertainty estimates. The prediction targets are regional fire events, not molecular structures, functions, designed sequences, or engineered assemblies.
examples.label: off_interest
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce a forest fire risk predictor and validate it prospectively at independent sites with rigorous uncertainty estimates.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce and externally validate an environmental risk predictor
examples.rationale: Strong validation cannot change an environmental prediction target into molecular design relevance.

examples.title: Fictional preliminary design of enzyme variants
examples.abstract: We design new enzyme variants with specified molecular binding properties, reporting only a preliminary computational demonstration. No independent experiment or held-out family evaluation is provided, so the supplied validation claim is weak despite the explicit engineering contribution.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We design new enzyme variants with specified molecular binding properties, reporting only a preliminary computational demonstration.
examples.contribution_object: Designed enzyme variants and binding properties
examples.contribution_task: Engineer molecular variants with preliminary computational evidence
examples.rationale: The scope is molecular engineering, while limited validation must remain a separate quality judgment.

examples.title: Fictional native protein study with no new predictor
examples.abstract: We do not introduce a protein predictor; we apply an existing predictor to describe a native enzyme. The supplied contribution is interpretation of this natural system, with no transferable method evaluation.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We do not introduce a protein predictor; we apply an existing predictor to describe a native enzyme.
examples.contribution_task: Apply an existing predictor without introducing a method
examples.rationale: The new-method phrase is explicitly negated and cannot supply positive contribution evidence.

examples.title: Fictional new predictor despite a negated application claim
examples.abstract: We do not merely apply an existing predictor; we introduce a transferable model that predicts molecular functions for unseen protein families. The study evaluates the new molecular predictor, so the negation attaches to mere application rather than to introduction.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We do not merely apply an existing predictor; we introduce a transferable model that predicts molecular functions for unseen protein families.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce a new predictor rather than merely apply one
examples.rationale: A sentence containing negation can still assert a distinct positive contribution in another clause.

examples.title: Fictional native mechanism motivating a future predictor
examples.abstract: We characterize a native enzyme mechanism and explain its observed conformational changes. In future work, we will develop a transferable protein conformation predictor; that planned method is not a result of the present study.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We characterize a native enzyme mechanism and explain its observed conformational changes.
examples.contribution_task: Explain observed natural behavior while planning a later method
examples.rationale: A future prediction-method claim does not change the completed natural-mechanism contribution.

examples.title: Fictional present contribution of a conformation predictor
examples.abstract: We develop and evaluate a transferable protein conformation predictor in the present study. The reported method predicts molecular behavior across families, while a future extension to other molecule types is described separately.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We develop and evaluate a transferable protein conformation predictor in the present study.
examples.contribution_task: Develop and evaluate a current molecular prediction method
examples.rationale: Future extensions should not erase a clearly completed present contribution.

examples.title: Fictional application of a previously introduced model
examples.abstract: Previous work introduced a transferable protein structure model. Here we apply that existing model to describe a single native protein complex, without adding a new predictor or a transferable evaluation protocol.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: Here we apply that existing model to describe a single native protein complex, without adding a new predictor or a transferable evaluation protocol.
examples.contribution_task: Apply a prior method to a descriptive case study
examples.rationale: The introduction belongs to previous work rather than to the present authors' contribution.

examples.title: Fictional own predictor contrasted with earlier methods
examples.abstract: Previous approaches used an existing predictor, whereas here we introduce a new molecular function model evaluated across held-out protein families. The contrast assigns the new prediction method to this study, rather than to the prior approaches.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: Previous approaches used an existing predictor, whereas here we introduce a new molecular function model evaluated across held-out protein families.
examples.contribution_object: Molecular functions across held-out protein families
examples.contribution_task: Introduce an own prediction method contrasted with prior tools
examples.rationale: Past-tense background and a present contribution can coexist in the same sentence.

examples.title: Fictional protein design workflow with unspecified ownership
examples.abstract: We investigate a protein design workflow and report promising results. The supplied abstract does not specify whether the workflow is newly introduced or merely applied, what molecular outputs are generated, or whether a new engineered system is the contribution.
examples.label: uncertain
examples.contribution_quote: The supplied abstract does not specify whether the workflow is newly introduced or merely applied, what molecular outputs are generated, or whether a new engineered system is the contribution.
examples.contribution_object: Unspecified outputs of a protein design workflow
examples.contribution_task: Unspecified contribution ownership and molecular output
examples.rationale: Domain words and promising results cannot resolve missing ownership and output information.

examples.title: Fictional protein design workflow with explicit ownership
examples.abstract: We introduce a new protein design workflow that generates molecular sequences with specified structural objectives. The workflow and its transfer across held-out design tasks are evaluated as the contribution, making ownership and molecular outputs explicit.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce a new protein design workflow that generates molecular sequences with specified structural objectives.
examples.contribution_task: Introduce and evaluate a molecular design workflow
examples.rationale: The abstract explicitly states a new workflow and its molecular design outputs.

examples.title: Fictional engineered RNA system made with an existing tool
examples.abstract: We use an existing design tool to engineer a new RNA nanostructure with a specified geometry and measured mechanical response. The tool is not new; the deliberately designed and characterized molecular system is the contribution.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We use an existing design tool to engineer a new RNA nanostructure with a specified geometry and measured mechanical response.
examples.contribution_task: Engineer and characterize a new molecular system using an existing tool
examples.rationale: Using an existing tool does not negate an explicit new molecular engineering contribution.

examples.title: Fictional native RNA description using an existing tool
examples.abstract: We use an existing folding tool to describe a naturally occurring RNA structure and interpret its native behavior. No engineered RNA architecture or transferable folding method is introduced; the contribution is a descriptive application to this molecule.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We use an existing folding tool to describe a naturally occurring RNA structure and interpret its native behavior.
examples.contribution_task: Describe native molecular behavior with an existing tool
examples.rationale: Tool use alone supplies no designed system or transferable method contribution.

examples.title: Fictional planned protein design method without reported results
examples.abstract: We plan to introduce a protein design method that will generate sequences with desired molecular structures. This supplied abstract describes the intended future study but gives no completed method, engineered molecular system, or reported evaluation.
examples.label: uncertain
examples.contribution_quote: This supplied abstract describes the intended future study but gives no completed method, engineered molecular system, or reported evaluation.
examples.contribution_object: Planned protein design outputs, not reported outputs
examples.contribution_task: Plan a future design study without an established completed contribution
examples.rationale: A planned study alone cannot establish the role or results of a completed research contribution.

examples.title: Fictional delivered protein design method
examples.abstract: We introduce and evaluate a protein design method that generates sequences with desired molecular structures. The supplied results compare generated systems across held-out design tasks, establishing a completed molecular design contribution rather than a future plan.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We introduce and evaluate a protein design method that generates sequences with desired molecular structures.
examples.contribution_task: Deliver and evaluate a molecular design method
examples.rationale: A completed current method must be distinguished from a proposal containing the same domain words.

examples.title: Fictional transferable evaluation of existing protein predictors
examples.abstract: We apply existing protein structure predictors to independently held-out families and establish a transferable evaluation of their generalization failures. The contribution is a systematic molecular prediction assessment across families, even though the underlying predictors are not newly introduced.
examples.label: core
examples.contribution_quote: We apply existing protein structure predictors to independently held-out families and establish a transferable evaluation of their generalization failures.
examples.contribution_object: Generalization of molecular structure predictors across families
examples.contribution_task: Meaningfully evaluate transferable molecular prediction performance
examples.rationale: Transferable evaluation of molecular predictors can be core without introducing a new predictor.

examples.title: Fictional isolated description with an existing protein predictor
examples.abstract: We apply an existing protein structure predictor to a single native enzyme and explain the observed structural arrangement. The study does not assess predictor generalization across families; its contribution is the description of this natural system.
examples.label: context
examples.contribution_quote: We apply an existing protein structure predictor to a single native enzyme and explain the observed structural arrangement.
examples.contribution_task: Describe one natural structure using an existing predictor
examples.rationale: An isolated descriptive application differs from a transferable method evaluation.
